Welcome to Stonehouse Park Federation
Perseverance, Aspiration, Responsibility, Kindness
Stonehouse Park Federation is a vibrant, inclusive learning community dedicated to ensuring every child achieves their full potential. We encourage kindness and tolerance among all our students. Pupils are inspired to confidently pursue their aspirations and learn perseverance by viewing challenges as opportunities for growth. Together, they take responsibility and become caring and active citizens who positively impact the world.
Our values and school rules are linked. They are developed to create positive relationships between staff and pupils. We expect good behaviour and attitudes to learning, supported through developed systems of rewards and celebrations.
We celebrate pupils in the following ways:
Every Child Needs a Champion - this video encapsulates every we stand for here at Park Federation.
If you would like to look around our wonderful schools to see our spacious learning environments and wonderful pupils, please contact the school office to arrange a convenient time.
We can’t wait to meet you

Information for Parents
Partnership with parents
Parents and carers are a child’s first educator, they know their children better than anyone. Which is why at Stonehouse Park Nursery we strive to work in partnership with our children’s parent and carers from the very beginning.
Stay and Plays
Before your child starts we will invite your family along to a stay and play. Where you will get the opportunity to meet the staff, including your child’s key worker and share valuable information about your child with them.
Online Journals
We use online journals to share some of your child’s learning at nursery. The journals allow you to access photo’s, video’s and statements of what they are learning at nursery. Giving you the opportunity to revisit that learning at home. It’s also great to share your child’s experiences outside of nursery, helping us to know your child better.
Regular phone calls
Once a term you will get a phone call update form your child’s key worker. Informing you of their progress, what they are enjoying and if there is anything we feel they need support with. It also gives you the chance to ask any questions and inform us of changes or upcoming events.
Face to face meetings
We also offer face to face meetings throughout the year, you can also request these at any point by emailing the nursery. These are usually 15 minute appointments with your child’s keyworker, we can include the nursery Senco if needed.

pageCache.pageTitle: School Hours , Term Dates and Wrap Around Care - Stonehouse Park Federation
pageCache.text:
School Hours, Term Dates and Wrap Around Care
Stonehouse Park Infant School is open from 8:55am – 3:15pm. Gates open at 8:45am.
Park Junior School is open from 8:50am – 3:20pm. Gates open at 8:40am.
Stonehouse Park Infants are taking part in the Governments Pilot Scheme for free breakfast clubs.
There is a breakfast club available in both schools from 7:30am and it costs £4.80 for infant children and £5.82 for junior children. ( The costs reflect the 30 minutes of free breakfast club time for the infant children). We hope to extend this to junior chidlren in the future.
There is an After School Club for children aged 2 – 14 based on the Infant School Site. It is open until 5:30pm and costs £11.65 a session.
Please note that if children are not booked in ahead of attending then there is a £1.10 admin charge per session.
Club places are booked online using ParentPay. The school admin team are happy to help you set this up the first time you use it.

Nursery Curriculum
Our nursery operates on the principle of "learning through play," as we believe this is the most meaningful way for young children to learn. We structure our day to include extended periods of uninterrupted play, allowing children to become deeply engaged in their own learning. We take great care in creating a rich and enabling environment, both indoors and outdoors, that fosters independence and cultivates a lifelong love of learning.
As the year progresses, our curriculum evolves to incorporate a balanced mix of motivating adult-led activities, core experiences, and targeted sessions tailored to each child’s needs. This dynamic approach ensures that we meet the developmental needs and interests of every child while laying a strong foundation for their future education.
Our curriculum is designed to give children the foundational knowledge and understanding needed to prepare them for reception. This is based on the Early Years Foundation Stage Statutory Framework and ‘Development Matters’ guidance, along with children’s interests and developmental needs.
A key priority in our nursery, as well as in our school, is the development of children’s language and vocabulary. We pride ourselves on creating a language-rich environment where communication skills are nurtured through meaningful interactions, carefully chosen stories, and a variety of songs and rhymes. We provide ample opportunities for children to become familiar with these elements, ensuring their language development is both natural and enjoyable.
Safeguarding and child welfare
At Stonehouse park nursery safeguarding is incorporated in all that we do, from our safer recruitment process to how the building is secured; child protection is part of our daily nursery routine. Your child’s welfare is our number one priority.
We have two ‘designated safeguard leads’ within the nursery. Whilst all nursery staff members are vigilant in their duty of care, it is the Designated person's responsibility to ensure staff members are up to date with the latest safeguarding updates, as well as to take the lead with any areas of concern.​
All staff members are DBS
Visitors to the nursery are always accompanied.

Attendance
Why is it important to come to school every day?
Coming to school every day is very important for your child.
Research has shown that children with poor attendance
Children who miss school miss out on valuable learning. Success in school is directly related to good attendance. The better the attendance the better the achievement. It is also very important that children get into good habits about coming to school every day right from the start.
Obviously children should not come to school if they are unwell. They need to stay at home and rest to get well. They also need to stay at home so they don’t pass on illness to others. This is particularly important if they have had a tummy bug. Public Health England advise that children should not come back to school for 48 hours after their last bout vomiting or diarrhoea. If children have poor attendance due to lots of illness we will recommend a referral to the school nurse or paediatrician to ensure there are no underlying health issues which need to be addressed.
The following reasons are not acceptable for missing school
Any child with attendance less than 90% is classed as having ‘persistent absence’. Good attendance is over 95%. If your child is away for more than 9 days a year they will not have good attendance.
We believe that it is vitally important for children to attend school for the following reasons:
By keeping a child out of school we are stopping them from experiencing and gaining these important things.
Research shows us that young people who regularly miss school without good reason are more likely to become isolated from their friends, to underachieve in examinations and become involved in anti-social behaviour.
A child’s education is very important, so the law is strong when it comes to helping a child receive their entitlement to it. Where we have concerns about a child’s attendance we always do our best to work with parents, to offer support to overcome the reasons behind poor attendance. However, when parents are not prepared to work with us we will inform the local authority which could result in legal action.
Why is it important to come to school on time every day?
Of course, it is better to be late coming to school than not coming to school at all. However, we always encourage punctuality at school. Not only is it a good habit to learn from an early age as ‘learning for life’ skill but also being on time is important for every child because
By regularly arriving late children can miss out on a lot of learning time

School Council
Pupil voice is highly regarded within school. One of the ways pupils can express their ideas is via the School Council.
Each class across the age ranges, starting from Year 1 through to Year 6, have one main councillor that has been elected by their peers and one deputy councillor; this allows more children the opportunity to be involved.
The children are enthusiastic members and are keen to fulfil their role as a councillor, brining suggestions and ideas gathered from their classes to the meeting to help improve their school community for the better.
